variances.meaning: قطّعته وفرّقته؛ عند ابن فارس مشبَّه بالحبّ المسمى الخردل، وهو اسم اتفق فيه العرب والعجم، موضوعٌ من غير اشتقاق
variances.meaning_english: I cut up and scattered the meat; likened to the seed called mustard (خردل), a word Arabs and non-Arabs happened to agree on, coined without derivation
made with dhāl substituting for dāl (a variant spelling)

variances.meaning: الذي يتطيّر، والميم زائدة، لأنه إذا تطيّر خَثِرَ وأقام
variances.meaning_english: one who takes bad omens (and so stops/hesitates); the mīm is an extra letter, because when he takes an omen he 'thickens/settles' (خَثِرَ) and stays put
variances.citation: ولستُ بهيّابٍ إذا شدّ رحلَه ... يقول عداني اليومَ واقٍ وحاتمُ

entries.core_meaning: باب ماجاء من كلام العرب على أكثر من ثلاثة أحرف أوله خاء (تتمة)
entries.core_meaning_english: Continuation of the appendix chapter on extended/blended words beginning with خ.
entries.notes: Continuation of the same appendix chapter (poem opening 'ولكنني أمضي...' continues the الأخثارم verse; footnote 1 attributes it to خُثيم بن عدي, known as الرقاش الكلابي, citing الحيوان وحواشيه 3:437/4). A stray marginal number '٢٢٢' appears mid-entry for الخنثعبة in the source image — recorded but excluded from the transcribed meaning. Footnote (3) flags a manuscript reading issue for الأخضارع: the base text may read with a different letter, and the editor corrects it to ض (dotted dād) per الجمهرة (2:394) واللسان والقاموس. Footnote (4) cites اللسان's (and الجمهرة/القاموس's) gloss 'البخيل المتسمح وتأبى شيمته السماحة' for البخيل المتسمح, with a corroborating verse — it does NOT cite al-Māwardī (the prior extraction's attribution to al-Māwardī is unsupported by the page and has been removed).

variances.meaning: الحديث الرقيق. ويقال خَلْبَسَ قلبَه: فتنه. منحوتةٌ من كلمتين: خلب وخلس
variances.meaning_english: fine/subtle speech; also 'khalbasa his heart' meaning he bewitched/enchanted it; blended from خلب (to beguile) and خلس (to snatch)

variances.meaning: الناقة الغزيرة؛ منحوتة من خَنَثَ وثَعَبَ، فكأنها لِبِنَة أخلفت يثعب باللبن ثعباً
variances.meaning_english: a she-camel copious in milk; blended from خنث and ثعب, as if she were a promised udder that gushes forth milk in a gush

variances.meaning: قالوا هو البخيل؛ فإن كان صحيحاً فهو من خضع وضرع، والبخيل كذا وصفه
variances.meaning_english: said to mean the miser; if correct, formed from خضع (to submit/abase oneself) and ضرع (to plead/entreat), because that is how the miser is described (he abases himself when asked to give)

variances.meaning: يقال هي الدنيا؛ وكل شيء يتلوّن ولا يدوم على حال؛ والمرأة السيئة الأخلاق؛ والشيطان؛ منحوتة من خَتَرَ وخَتَعَ
variances.meaning_english: said of worldly life (fickle, never lasting); anything that keeps changing colour and never stays on one state is 'khaytaʿūr'; also the ill-natured woman, and the devil; blended from ختر (treachery) and ختع (a kind of guile/running)

variances.meaning: الشابّة الرخصة الحسنة القوام؛ منحوتة من اخرعّ (اللِّين) والرَّعبوبة (الناعمة). ويقال: جملٌ خُرْعُوبٌ: طويلٌ في حسن خَلْقٍ. وغُصْنٌ خُرْعُوبٌ: متثنٍّ
variances.meaning_english: a soft, well-formed young woman; blended from اخرعّ (suppleness) and رعبوبة (softness/tenderness). Also used of a camel: tall and well-formed; and of a branch: supple/bending
variances.citation: بَرَهْرَهَةٍ رُؤْدَةٍ رَخْصَةٍ ... كخُرْعُوبَةِ البانَةِ المُنْفَطِرْ (لامرئ القيس، ديوانه ص٨؛ اللسان: خرب، خرع، بره) — the verse's second hemistich prints at the top of the following page (816).

entries.core_meaning: باب ماجاء من كلام العرب على أكثر من ثلاثة أحرف أوله خاء (تتمة)
entries.core_meaning_english: Continuation of the appendix chapter on extended/blended words beginning with خ.
entries.notes: Continuation; opens with the tail end (second hemistich) of the خرعوب poem citation carried over from the previous page. Footnote (1) attributes the full verse to Imruʼ al-Qays (ديوانه ص٨) and cross-references اللسان (خرب، خرع، بره); it also quotes the first hemistich 'برهرهة رؤدة رخصة'. Footnote (2) glosses الأخرات as plural of خرت (the ear's perforation/hole) and flags a manuscript correction 'أخراتها' vs 'أخراسها' (the latter a scribal error). Footnote (3) attributes the خلبص verse to the poet لبيد المري (Lubayd al-Murri, not merely 'a transmitter of Lubayd'), per اللسان (خلص). No explicit close-of-chapter marker appears on this page, so it is uncertain from these three pages alone whether the chapter ends here.

variances.meaning: أفسده؛ منحوتة من خَرِبَ وخَرِقَ. والأخرق: الذي لا يُحسن عمله. وخَرَبَه: إذا ثقبه
variances.meaning_english: he ruined/spoiled his work; blended from خرب (to be ruined) and خرق (to be clumsy/inept) — the clumsy man does not do his work well; and 'kharabahu' also means he pierced/holed it

variances.meaning: من الكلام الذي لا يتأوّل على مثله ولا وجه للاشتغال به
variances.meaning_english: the term for the male spider — Ibn Fāris says this word admits no such derivational explanation and is not worth pursuing

variances.meaning: الباء زائدة، لأن الخُرْص هو الحلقة
variances.meaning_english: an earring; the bāʼ is an extra letter, because الخُرص means 'the ring'
variances.citation: جُمِّلَتْ في أَخراتِها خَرْبَصِيصاً ... من جُمانٍ قد زان وجهاً جميلاً

variances.meaning: إذا فرّ؛ الباء فيه زائدة، وهو من خَلَصَ
variances.meaning_english: he fled/escaped; the bāʼ is an extra letter; from خلص (to get free/escape)
variances.citation: لمّا رآني بالبِرازِ حَصْحَصا ... في الأرض منّي هَرَباً وخَلْبَصا

variances.meaning: اختلاط الأمر؛ فإن كان صحيحاً فالنون زائدة، وإنما هو من خبص، وبه سمّي الخبيص
variances.meaning_english: confusion/mixing-up of a matter; if correct, the nūn is an extra letter, and it derives from خبص (to mix), the same root that names the sweet dish الخبيص

variances.meaning: معروف، والراء زائدة، والأصل فيه الخطم. فأما الخمر فقد تسمّى بذلك، ويقولون: هو أول ما يسيل عند العصر، فإن كان كذا فهو قياس الباب لأن الأول متقدّم
variances.meaning_english: well-known word (the trunk/snout); the rāʼ is an extra letter, the base being خطم (snout); wine too is called by this name, since they say it is the first liquid to flow when pressing — if so, that fits the chapter's core sense of 'that which comes first'

variances.meaning: من ذلك اشتقاق الخَطْم والخِطام. ومن الباب تسميتهم سادة القوم الخراطيمَ
variances.meaning_english: from this same root come الخطم and الخطام (the halter/nose-rein); and from this chapter, Arabs call the chiefs/leaders of a people 'al-kharāṭīm' (the noses/foremost ones)

entries.core_meaning: أي ظَلَعٌ، وهذه منحوتة من كلمتين: من خَزَل أي قطع، وخَزَع أي قطع، وقد مضى
entries.core_meaning_english: limping/lameness; a blend of two words, khazala (to cut/sever) and khaza'a (to cut/sever), both already discussed earlier

variances.meaning_english: a she-camel with a limp

entries.notes: Corrected core_meaning wording: page reads 'وقد مضى' (already passed/discussed), not 'وقد مرّا' as in the prior extraction.

entries.core_meaning: وممّا اشتُقّ اشتقاقاً قولهم للثقيل الوخيم القبيح: الفحج (خفنجل)، وهذا إنما هو من الفحج وقد مضى، لأنهم إذا أرادوا تشنيعاً وتقبيحاً زادوا في الاسم
entries.core_meaning_english: a term coined by derivation for a coarse, ungainly, unpleasant (bow-legged) person; built on 'faḥaj' (bow-leggedness, already discussed), with extra letters added for emphasis/ugliness of the description
entries.notes: Corrected root_letters to include the lām, which is part of the headword's own skeleton (خفنجل) — the prior extraction dropped it without textual basis; only the nūn-infix pattern is implied by analogy elsewhere in this appendix, and even that is not explicitly named here. Footnote: original text reads 'التقل' where editor suggests correction to 'الثقيل'.

entries.core_meaning: وأما قولهم للقديم خنابس فوضعٌ أيضاً لا يُعرف اشتقاقه
entries.core_meaning_english: their word for 'the old/ancient' — also a base-coined form whose derivation is unknown

variances.meaning_english: the old/ancient one
variances.citation: أبى اللهُ أن أُخزَى وعِزٌّ خُنابِسُ

entries.notes: Closes 'تم كتاب الخاء' (the end of the khā' book). Footnote attributes the verse to al-Zubayr's line 'وقالوا عليك ابن الزبير فلذ به', from the dīwān of al-Quṭāmī.
